page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It is built on the Intel x86_64 architecture and provides 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 384 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU resources are available on this server configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2411.16 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1471.0. However, multi-core scaling is limited, as shown by a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 4280.0 and a weak bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 23.47 GB/sec. Memory performance also exhibits a significant divergence: cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 497.33 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the weak category at 35.47 GB/sec and 17.49 GB/sec respectively.

The shared CPU allocation model introduces potential resource contention, which represents a key tradeoff for this instance. This is reflected in weaker database and multi-threaded benchmark results, such as a PassMark database operations score of 2003.37. Qualitatively, this server represents a cost-effective option for workloads requiring a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio and fast local NVMe storage, without the higher cost associated with dedicated CPU threads.

This server configuration is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, Redis key-value caching, and lightweight single-threaded processing tasks. It is less suitable for intensive database operations, complex multi-threaded software compilation, or large-scale data processing due to its shared CPU architecture and lower uncached memory throughput.
